li.label: a name for mercy
li.description: A traveler had heard that we spare the raiders we beat. Strange thing to be known for, but I'll take it.

li.label: known as soft
li.description: On the road they say we patch up raiders and send them home. They're laughing at us.

li.label: a kindness came back
li.description: We let a prisoner go once. Today a trader remembered it and paid us back in herbs and silver.

li.label: they fear us
li.description: A visitor pulled a child away from me today. I was only going to wave.

li.label: feared on the road
li.description: The visitors keep their children close when I walk by. Good. Let them.

li.label: frightened a trader
li.description: The trader gave us a better price because they were afraid of us. That doesn't sit right with me.

li.label: a frightened trader's price
li.description: I didn't even have to haggle. The trader was afraid of us and kept lowering the price.

li.label: fed a traveler
li.description: A traveler went out of their way because they'd heard we'd feed them. We fed them twice.

li.label: another mouth at the door
li.description: Every hungry traveler on the road knows where our kitchen is now. Our stores won't last.

li.label: spoken well of
li.description: Folk on the road still talk about what we gave away. I like being that kind of place.

li.label: known for hard bargains
li.description: The trader expected a fight over every piece of silver, and got one.

li.label: called a miser
li.description: A trader haggled with me like I was a known cheat. Apparently we're known as misers.

li.label: proved a point
li.description: A guest brought their own bread because they'd heard we wouldn't share. I shared mine, mostly out of spite.

li.label: our ways praised
li.description: An old traveler said we keep the old customs better than anywhere else on the road.

li.label: a guest who knew our ways
li.description: The trader waited at the gate for bread and salt, the proper way. Hardly anyone remembers to anymore.

li.label: showed off our new ideas
li.description: A traveler came all this way to see what we're trying here. I could have talked about it all day.

li.label: nothing where it was
li.description: The trader couldn't find the storeroom because we'd moved it again. That's what we're like, and I like it.

li.label: guests at ease
li.description: The visitors took their boots off and sang with us half the night.

li.label: trusted with the road's news
li.description: The trader told me news they don't share with just anyone, because we always let them in.

li.label: guests afraid to move
li.description: A visitor asked my permission to walk to the well. I don't like that we've become that kind of place.

li.label: guests minding their manners
li.description: The visitors kept their hands where we could see them. That's how it should be.

li.label: opened the gate a little
li.description: I let a trader in past the watch instead of haggling through the gate. The sky didn't fall.

li.label: the work was noticed
li.description: A trader stopped to stare at our fields, without a weed in them. People on the road know how hard we work.

li.label: an idle hour
li.description: A visitor made me sit down and rest for a while. I'd forgotten how. I might do it again next year.

li.label: the envy of travelers
li.description: A traveler saw how we live, with our long lunches and no work bells, and wished they could stay. We have something good here.

li.label: thought idle
li.description: Travelers think we're lazy here. I work, and I'd like that noted somewhere.

li.label: no hurry
li.description: A trader had to wait on us for a while. We do things in our own time here.

li.label: kept a trader waiting
li.description: A trader waited half a day for us to get around to them. I'd have had the deal done and a fence mended by then.

li.label: gave someone sanctuary
li.description: They came to us because they'd heard we were merciful, and we took them in. I'm proud of that.

li.label: we took in a runaway
li.description: A runaway came to us from their own people, and we didn't send them back.

li.label: gave a runaway back
li.description: The runaway trusted me, and the council handed them straight back to the people they were running from.

li.label: we gave them up
li.description: We told their masters where the runaway had gone. They trusted us, and now they're paying for it.

li.label: betrayed to my own people
li.description: I asked them for help, and they told the people I was hiding from. So much for their mercy.

li.label: a night's rest
li.description: They couldn't take me in, but they gave me a warm corner and a full bowl for the night.

li.label: sent them back on the road
li.description: We gave the runaway a night's rest and a full bowl, then sent them on. It wasn't what they asked for.

li.label: not so soft after all
li.description: I'd heard this place was soft on prisoners. Now there's a new guard on my door.

li.label: nobody's fool
li.description: The prisoner thought our mercy meant we were weak. They know better now.

li.label: hard on a prisoner
li.description: A prisoner made a joke about our mercy, so we came down hard on them. That's petty.

li.label: taken for fools
li.description: The prisoner laughed at our mercy, and the council let them go anyway.

li.label: mercy sent out
li.description: We sent food to people who are afraid of us, and asked nothing back. Maybe the stories about us will change.

li.label: gone soft
li.description: We're going easy on people who used to fear us. That fear kept us safe.

li.label: silver instead
li.description: The council sent silver instead of food. It's not what I asked for, but it's something.

li.label: still the place they fear
li.description: I asked for one kind thing. The council said our name is doing its job.

li.label: known for cruelty
li.description: People out there use our name to frighten children, and the council is content with that.

li.label: flogged by strangers
li.description: My own people handed me over to strangers to be whipped, because these strangers are known for it. My back is raw.

li.label: held the whip
li.description: They held the whip. I won't forget their face.

li.label: held the whip
li.description: The visitors asked for me by name to do the whipping, and I did it. I can still hear it.

li.label: kept our name
li.description: They came all this way to see us do it properly, and we did.

li.label: a flogging in our yard
li.description: We whipped somebody else's thief in our yard, just because they asked us to.

li.label: spared by strangers
li.description: My own people wanted me whipped. These strangers, the hard ones from the stories, untied my hands instead.

li.label: could have, didn't
li.description: They had the whip in hand and every excuse to use it. They didn't.

li.label: put the whip down
li.description: They handed me a whip and expected me to use it. The council said no, and I was glad.

li.label: nobody turned away
li.description: Anyone who comes hungry to our gate gets fed. I'm proud of that, even when the larder runs low.

li.label: feeding the whole road
li.description: Every hungry traveler for three valleys knows the way to our kitchen. Our stores are going out the gate one bowl at a time.

li.label: food for work
li.description: Anyone who wants a bowl splits wood first. That's fair, and the woodpile has never been bigger.

li.label: the gate closed to the hungry
li.description: We used to feed anyone who came hungry. Now we turn them away at the gate.

li.label: no more handouts
li.description: The food we grow stays with the people who grow it. About time.

li.label: an unexpected gift
li.description: Their colony is known for being stingy, but this one sent me off with a full purse.

li.label: saved face
li.description: The trader called us misers, so we sent them off with a generous gift. That'll give them something to talk about.

li.label: silver for a joke
li.description: We paid a trader good silver just to stop laughing at us. Most expensive joke I've ever heard.

li.label: laughed at for our thrift
li.description: A trader made fools of us at the gate, and the council let it stand. My ears are still burning.

li.label: thrifty and proud
li.description: Let them laugh. Our silver stays in our stores.

li.label: charged me for water
li.description: I made a joke about their stinginess, and they charged me two silver a bucket for water.

li.label: made it worse
li.description: I asked the council to shut the trader up, and they charged them for water instead. Now there's a new story about us on the road.

li.label: made to keep the custom
li.description: The council ordered me to keep a custom I don't believe in. So I keep it, loudly and badly.

li.label: the custom upheld
li.description: Some things here are older than any of us, and the council remembered that.

li.label: free to choose
li.description: The council said I can keep the custom or not, as I like. Now I'm half tempted to keep it.

li.label: the custom slighted
li.description: The council decided our customs are optional now. I wonder what else will turn out to be optional.

li.label: an old custom brought back
li.description: We did it the old way again, all of us at one table. I'd forgotten how much I missed it.

li.label: brought it back
li.description: I asked for one old thing to be kept, and the council said yes. For an evening it felt like home again.

li.label: an old custom, new again
li.description: We brought back the old evening, with a few new twists of our own.

li.label: not quite how it was
li.description: They brought the old custom back, more or less. It's not the same, but it's better than nothing.

li.label: the old ways let go
li.description: The council said we've outgrown it. Maybe we have. I hadn't.

li.label: a guest in my bed
li.description: The council says guests are guests. Mine is sleeping in my bed and drinking my beer.

li.label: made welcome
li.description: These people never tell you to leave. I could get used to it here.

li.label: the guest earned their keep
li.description: We handed our guest an axe. If they live like family, they can work like family.

li.label: got my bed back
li.description: The guests were shown the road and I got my bed back. It smells of someone else, but it's mine.

li.label: had me shown out
li.description: Their colony is supposed to be friendly, but this one had me walked off their land.

li.label: guests sent off
li.description: We sent a whole party of guests away because one of them borrowed some boots.

li.label: my old friend let in
li.description: The council opened the gate for my old friend. We ate at the same table, like before. I won't forget it.

li.label: let in at last
li.description: They don't usually let strangers in, but they let me in. My old friend must have begged.

li.label: the rules bent
li.description: The council let a stranger in because one of us asked nicely. I thought we had rules about that.

li.label: my friend kept outside
li.description: My oldest friend slept outside the walls with the pack animals, because rules are rules. I passed a blanket over the wall like a thief.

li.label: kept outside the walls
li.description: My friend lives behind those walls, and I slept outside them with the mules.

li.label: a night outside the walls
li.description: The gate stayed shut to my friend, so I went out to them. We talked until the fire burned down.

li.label: a day off
li.description: The council gave me a day off. I sat by the water and did nothing at all.

li.label: a day of rest
li.description: We all had a whole day with no work. The fields were fine without us.

li.label: a wasted day
li.description: A whole day without work. I sat on my hands and counted everything that wasn't getting done.

li.label: worked ragged
li.description: I asked for one day off, and they said the work won't wait. I'm worn to the bone.

li.label: the council backed me
li.description: The council has ordered the others to pull their weight. It took long enough.

li.label: put to work
li.description: The council says everyone pulls their weight now. Mine was resting, and it liked resting.

li.label: about time
li.description: Finally, we're all pulling our weight. I might even get a full night's sleep.

li.label: thanked at supper
li.description: They stood up at supper and thanked me by name for all the work I've been doing.

li.label: told to slow down
li.description: I told the council I was doing everyone's work, and they told me to do less. The fields won't tend themselves.
